definitions.gloss: covert operative; secret agent; undercover agent
definitions.explanation: A person sent by a state or organization to carry out clandestine activity — espionage, sabotage, or influence operations — in another country or group. Almost always used of the other side, never as a neutral job title.

examples.japanese: {工作員|こうさくいん}が{潜入|せんにゅう}していた。
examples.english: An operative had infiltrated the group.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{外国|がいこく}の{工作員|こうさくいん}だと{疑|うたが}われている。
examples.english: He is suspected of being a foreign agent.

examples.japanese: {工作員|こうさくいん}が{偽|いつわ}りの{情報|じょうほう}を{流|なが}して{世論|よろん}を{動|うご}かそうとしたらしい。
examples.english: Operatives apparently tried to sway public opinion by spreading false information.

notes:
Formed from {工作|こうさく} (maneuvering, covert operations) plus the suffix {員|いん} (member, staff). Note that {工作|こうさく} on its own also means "handicrafts" — the school subject — so the covert sense comes entirely from the compound and its context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {工作員|こうさくいん}を{送|おく}り{込|こ}む: to send in an operative
- {工作員|こうさくいん}が{潜入|せんにゅう}する: for an operative to infiltrate
- {産業|さんぎょう}{工作員|こうさくいん}: industrial spy

REGISTER:
The word carries a strong negative charge and is common in news reports and thrillers. Online it is also thrown around loosely as an insult, accusing someone of posting on behalf of a foreign government.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スパイ: spy — broader and more neutral; focuses on gathering information
- {諜報員|ちょうほういん}: intelligence agent — formal, specifically about intelligence work
